newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia urban unemployment rises to 12.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Colombia urban unemployment rises to 12.1 pct.

text.p: Colombia's urban unemployment rate rose to 12.1 percent of the workforce in September compared to 8.7 percent in September of last year, the National Statistics Department (DANE) said Thursday.

Edgar Alberto Santiago, DANE's director, told a news conference 665,886 workers in Colombia's seven leading cities were unemployed in September of this year compared to 495,745 in the same month last year.

The 3.4 percentage point increase in open unemployment comes against the backdrop of a sharp slowdown in economic growth and business and industrial activity over the past year, with cyclical factors aggravated by the political crisis stemming from the drug corruption scandal dogging President Ernesto Samper.
Santiago said a year-old slump in the construction sector was among the factors weighing heavily on urban employment.
According to DANE, Bogota was the city with the lowest unemployment rate in September, at 10.4, while the southwest city of Pasto had the highest rate, at 15.5 percent.
